Philanthropy

fih-LAN-thruh-pee -- built from Greek roots meaning 'love' and 'humankind.' · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Philanthropy is promoting the welfare of others through generous donations of money.

Her decades of philanthropy funded schools, hospitals, and libraries across the region.

Worked Example

A retired businessman quietly donates most of his fortune to build clean water wells in villages he will likely never visit himself.

That generous goodwill directed toward helping humanity, often through giving, is exactly what philanthropy describes. Unlike 'business,' which seeks profit, philanthropy seeks to help others without expecting anything back.

How Philanthropy Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

charity

charity: generosity toward those in need

generosity

generosity: the quality of being willing to give freely

benevolence

benevolence: the quality of being kind and charitable

Antonyms

selfishness

selfishness: a lack of concern for others, focused only on oneself

greed

greed: an intense desire for wealth beyond what one needs

How Strong Is It? — charity → philanthropy → benevolence

charity vs. philanthropy

charity vs. philanthropy: Charity is a more everyday word than philanthropy -- charity can describe any act of giving, large or small, while philanthropy often implies a larger, more organized, and sustained effort to help humanity.

benevolence vs. philanthropy

benevolence vs. philanthropy: Benevolence can feel broader than philanthropy: philanthropy specifically involves generous giving, often of money, while benevolence describes an overall kind and charitable character, whether or not money is involved.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — phil-

prefix — phil-: love, fondness for (Greek)

root — -anthrop-

root — -anthrop-: human, mankind (Greek (anthropos))

suffix — -y

suffix — -y: noun-forming ending (state, practice) (Greek (-ia))

Put it together

Put it together: Greek phil- ('love') plus anthropos ('human being') plus the noun ending -y names 'love of humankind' -- generosity aimed at people in general. The same anthrop- root gives us anthropology.

Use the root in a new word: anthropology

Use the root in a new word: anthropology: She spent her career studying anthropology, traveling the world to learn how different cultures live.
